case.title: Scheduled report exports: from customer request to production
case.trigger: Customers ask for reports sent automatically as CSV or PDF (Product)
case.end: Scheduled exports live in production and announced to customers (Product)

steps.name: Customer requests collected from support tickets and account reviews

ai.label: Claude clusters the tickets by theme

steps.name: Usage data checked: who exports reports today and how

wait.text: 2 days, waiting for a data extract

markers.text: Data extracts are requested by ticket to the data team

ai.label: Claude drafts the brief from the clustered tickets

wait.text: about 3 days, the PO is on other topics

ai.label: Claude proposes acceptance criteria from the brief

steps.name: Data access rules for scheduled exports

wait.text: 4 days, waiting for the security review slot

markers.text: One security reviewer for all teams, weekly slot

steps.name: Refinement meeting with dev and QA

wait.text: up to a week, next refinement session

steps.name: Technical notes on the report engine

ai.label: Claude reads the report engine and lists the impacted modules

wait.text: up to 2 weeks, the current sprint must end

markers.text: Ready stories wait for the next sprint

ai.label: Claude Code writes the scheduler and its tests from the technical notes

markers.text: Scheduler written in two days instead of a week

steps.name: Export dialog in the web app

ai.label: Claude Code builds the dialog from the Figma mock-ups

markers.text: PDF layout breaks on wide tables

ai.label: Claude writes the missing tests and runs them until green

steps.name: Automated review of the pull request

ai.label: Review agent comments the PR on style, security and tests

wait.text: about a day, reviewers are busy

markers.text: PRs wait for a senior reviewer

steps.name: Functional tests of exports (CSV, PDF, schedules)

ai.label: Claude generates Playwright tests from the acceptance criteria

steps.caSource: QA: about 4 stories in 10 come back incomplete

markers.text: Bugs are described twice, in Jira and in Slack

wait.text: up to a week, monthly train

markers.text: One release a month for all teams

ai.label: Claude drafts the release note from the merged PRs

loops.label: Stories sent back to Product when acceptance criteria are not testable
Back and forth with Claude on the scheduler
Bugs found in QA go back to dev
Feature incomplete on the test environment
A data access question surfaces late and goes back to Security

parking.text: An agent that runs the regression suite on every PR and posts the results
Weekly releases instead of the monthly train

hypotheses.text: Time is lost between teams more than in the work.
AI speeds up Build, but the work then waits longer in Review and QA.
Unclear acceptance criteria cause most of the rework.

log.text: Build detailed in four sub-steps; UI dialog in parallel with the API
QA rework loops added with their counts
Sprint planning kept as one box (not detailed); first Discovery step marked upstream
